Synergistic Interfacial Engineering in Strontium Perovskite-MXene Nanocomposite for Advanced Room-Temperature Gas Sensing

Abstract:

Industrial gas emission and air pollution has caused an urgent demand for highly sensitive, room-temperature-operable environmental and industrial safety monitoring. This thesis presents the strategic design of advanced chemiresistive gas sensors based on strontium-based perovskite oxide (ABO3) and two-dimensional Ti3C2TX MXene nanocomposites. By pairing oxygen-vacancy-rich perovskites with highly conductive MXene sheets, these material architectures overcome traditional charge-transport limitations through powerful interfacial synergy. The work systematically explores four core optimization strategies: utilizing spherical SrTiO3 nanoparticles for enhanced room-temperature NO2 detection tuning SrZrO3 morphologies to optimize surface-active sites for non-polar methane (CH4) sensing developing (Fe-substituted SrZrO3-MoS2-MXene) ternary hybrids to maximize catalytic edge sites for selective detection of SO2 and engineering B-site electronics via a Schottky-contacted SrFeO3-MXene interface towards detection of acetone. Furthermore, this work demonstrates how these optimized nanocomposites translate effectively into both durable rigid as well as flexible substrates for stationary industrial monitoring and wearable applications. To elucidate the underlying sensing mechanisms, detailed structural, textural, spectroscopic, microscopic, and electrochemical characterizations were systematically performed, establishing synergistically engineered room temperature gas sensors.
